title: c-VEP dataset from Thielen et al. (2015)
description: A 64-channel EEG dataset from 12 healthy participants using a broad-band visually evoked potential (BBVEP) brain-computer interface. The interface was a 6x6 matrix speller driven by modulated Gold codes. Participants completed three copy-spelling runs of 36 trials each. The original study used a reconvolution model to predict responses to unseen stimulation sequences and used them as templates for classification. It reached about 86% online accuracy.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a Biosemi ActiveTwo system (64 active electrodes, 2048 Hz) while participants attended target cells in a 6x6 speller flashing with modulated Gold codes (126 bits, 1.05 s per cycle). Each trial lasted 4.2 s (4 code cycles). Data were downsampled to 360 Hz, linearly de-trended, common-average referenced and spectrally filtered. Classification used template matching with correlation and canonical correlation analysis for spatial filtering.
